mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during downturns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during expansions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, the combination signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during inflationary periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 70% of instances with strong PAYEMS growth, or the correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3 percentage points, the combination signals a weakening consumer demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 1% and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strong construction sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and related industries benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during expansions.
